meta.about_government_approval: Australia approves Islamic organisations only for halal red meat exports. The Department of Agriculture's list of Approved Islamic Organisations (updated 8 July 2026) has 18 bodies, all included here. AFIC is added as a major domestic certifier that is not on that list. Domestic halal labelling is not government regulated.
meta.red_meat_note: For export red meat, the government halal program requires an authorised Muslim slaughterman to make the cut by hand, and allows only reversible stunning. Most Australian halal red meat is stunned; a few plants have state approval to skip stunning.
meta.poultry_note: Poultry is outside the government halal program. Most Australian halal chicken is machine-slaughtered after stunning. ANIC rejects CAS gas stunning; AFIC accepts it.
meta.disclaimer: Compiled from public sources on the date above. Most Australian certifiers publish no written slaughter standard; 'unknown' means no reliable public source was found. Confirm with the certifier before relying on any field.
